condition: Obstructive AKI from high-pressure chronic retention
permutationLabel: Elderly man, painless chronic retention, AKI stage 3
summary: 83-year-old man with dribbling incontinence, confusion and a painless bladder to the umbilicus; 1.6 L, bilateral hydronephrosis, creatinine 486, K 6.2.

inputs.hpi: Three weeks of dribbling incontinence and new bed-wetting at night, poor stream for years. Family noticed confusion and a swollen lower abdomen. Takes amitriptyline for neuropathic pain. No pain.

exam.general: Mildly confused, euvolaemic. Pulse 92/min, BP 168/92, RR 20, temperature 36.7°C.
exam.abdomen: Painless, dull, distended bladder palpable to the umbilicus. PR: smooth, enlarged benign-feeling prostate.

imaging.name: USS renal tract
imaging.result: Bladder volume 1.6 L; bilateral moderate hydronephrosis; normal renal size.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: High-pressure chronic urinary retention with obstructive AKI stage 3
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: High-pressure chronic retention (1.6 L, bilateral hydronephrosis) with AKI stage 3 (creatinine 486) and potassium 6.2.

mustInclude.note: After decompressing high-pressure chronic retention, diuresis can cause hypovolaemia and electrolyte loss.

mustInclude.knownGapNote: Web: Nephrology only; no urology referral.

Web: Amitriptyline is not recognised as a retention precipitant. | iOS CI 2026-09-25 (run 36169134350, database mode): no management item matched among 27 (ios.pipeline.actions, ios.radiation.plan, ios.radiation.referral, ios.radiation.followUp, ios.soap.plan)
mustInclude.proposedFix: Add anticholinergic drugs to a retention precipitant check.

mustExclude.note: High-pressure chronic retention: catheter until urological assessment; an early TWOC risks recurrent obstructive AKI (surgeon to confirm).

guideline.name: NICE NG148 — Acute kidney injury: prevention, detection and management
guideline.section: Detection (creatinine against baseline); urinalysis for all with AKI; ultrasound of the urinary tract within 24 h when obstruction is suspected (immediately if pyonephrosis suspected); stop/withhold nephrotoxic drugs (NSAIDs, ACE inhibitors, ARBs, diuretics) and review metformin; refer to urology immediately for pyonephrosis, obstructed solitary kidney, bilateral upper tract obstruction or complications of obstruction; nephrology referral criteria
guideline.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. Acute kidney injury: prevention, detection and management. NICE guideline NG148. London: NICE; 2019.

guideline.name: KDIGO Clinical Practice Guideline for Acute Kidney Injury
guideline.section: 2.1 Definition and staging (creatinine rise ≥26.5 µmol/L in 48 h or ≥1.5× baseline in 7 days, or urine output <0.5 mL/kg/h for 6 h; stage by creatinine ratio/urine output); 3.1 fluids and haemodynamic management; discontinue nephrotoxic agents; evaluate cause
guideline.citation: Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) Acute Kidney Injury Work Group. KDIGO Clinical Practice Guideline for Acute Kidney Injury. Kidney Int Suppl. 2012;2:1–138.

guideline.name: EAU Guidelines on the management of non-neurogenic male LUTS (acute urinary retention)
guideline.section: Acute urinary retention: bladder decompression by urethral (or suprapubic) catheter; alpha-blocker before trial without catheter; renal function; identify precipitants (anticholinergics, constipation)
guideline.citation: Gravas S, Gacci M, Gratzke C, et al. EAU Guidelines on Management of Non-Neurogenic Male LUTS. EAU Guidelines Office, Arnhem; 2024 edition.

guideline.name: NICE CG97 — Lower urinary tract symptoms in men: management
guideline.section: Acute urinary retention: offer an alpha blocker before catheter removal; chronic retention with renal impairment (high-pressure chronic retention): catheterise and refer to urology before bladder outflow surgery
guideline.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. Lower urinary tract symptoms in men: management. Clinical guideline CG97. London: NICE; 2010 (updated 2015).

rationale: Obstruction is the reversible AKI cause a surgeon must find. NICE NG148 / CG97: catheterise, watch for post-obstructive diuresis, urology.
